summary: This joint resolution nullifies the EPA's January 2025 rule that waived federal preemption for California's Omnibus Low NOx motor vehicle and engine emissions standards.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a Congressional Review Act resolution disapproving an EPA emissions rule. It contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budgets.
The legislation addresses only the validity of an EPA regulatory waiver and has no tax-related content.
No provisions touch on healthcare policy, insurance, or medical regulation.
The bill is unrelated to firearms or gun regulations.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions are present.
The resolution does not address reproductive health or abortion policy.
No military, defense, or national security spending or policy elements exist.

The bill uses the CRA to nullify an EPA decision granting California a waiver for its Omnibus Low NOx vehicle emissions regulation. This directly prevents implementation of stricter state-level pollution controls on motor vehicles, thereby limiting environmental regulation.
No welfare, entitlement, or social assistance programs are addressed.
The legislation contains nothing related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance provisions appear.
The bill does not affect sentencing, policing, or criminal justice procedures.
No trade agreements, tariffs, or import/export rules are involved.
The resolution has no fiscal or debt implications.
No civil rights or LGBTQ-related legal protections are addressed.
The bill does not mention foreign assistance or international aid.
No election administration, voting access, or campaign provisions exist.
The legislation is silent on technology regulation, data privacy, or internet policy.
No labor, union, or workplace rights provisions are included.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
